instructions: Heat the oven to its lowest setting for 10 minutes (about 120°F), then turn it off.
In a large glass or plastic bowl, stir together the flour, yeast and sugar. Whisk in 1 cup of lukewarm water and the salt until you have a loose, sticky batter.
Cover the bowl with a damp tea towel and put it in the warm oven. Leave it until the batter has doubled, about 1 hour.

Pour the olive oil and vegetable oil into a heavy pot, about 2 inches deep. Heat over medium until it reaches 320°F. No thermometer? Drop in a little batter. It should sizzle gently, float up and turn golden in about 2 minutes.

Set a bowl of cold water and a cooling rack with paper towels underneath beside the stove. Dip a teaspoon in the water, scoop up a small spoonful of batter and push it into the oil with a second wet teaspoon.
Fry 6 to 8 at a time, turning them with two forks, for about 3 minutes, until golden all over. Don't crowd the pot.
Transfer the loukoumades to the rack to drain. Repeat with the rest of the batter.
Warm the honey in a small pan over low heat until it pours easily. Drizzle it over the loukoumades and dust with the cinnamon. Serve warm.
advance_prep_notes: the batter needs about 1 hour to rise before frying
method_notes: No version has 20 ratings, so this follows Real Greek Recipes (4.06 from 17), halved: a flour, water, yeast and sugar batter, no egg or milk, fried in a mix of olive and vegetable oil. Taste of Home and Eleni Saltas agree on a sticky batter that rises about an hour and a half. The honey drizzle and amount are from Taste of Home. Walnuts and other nuts are left off to keep it nut-free. Makes about 20.
